text:
samir: FYI canary v5.0.2 at 20% in eu-central is showing intermittent 502s on /chat, started ~5m ago :confused:
deploy-bot: rollout: v5.0.2 -> 20% eu-central. metrics snapshot: 502=1.8% (baseline 0.02%), p95=360ms. autorevert rule: 5xx>1% sustained 3m. breach detected 2m ago.
claire: that's above our auto threshold. is this spread across instances or concentrated?
samir: looks concentrated to a subset of pods behind a single node pool (nodepool-alpha). logs show "bad response from model-variant" errors.
ops-ray: could be a model-load failure for the new variant. we can try targeted traffic-shift off the failing pods to fallback variant before full rollback. less impact than full revert.
pm-leo: if we shift, customer comms need to mention partial fallback. prefer to pin and triage first.
samir: pinning at 20% and applying manual hold now. deploy-bot: traffic pinned at 20% by samir; autopilot rollback suppressed.
sre-alex: proposing plan: 1) cordon failing node, 2) shift 50% of canary traffic to model-variant v5.0.1-fallback on the same rollout group, 3) monitor 5xx for 6m, 4) if stable, resume. If not, rollback to v5.0.1.
claire: do we have runtime support for variant-level routing in this rollout?
ops-ray: yes, route-split supports per-model-variant weight. will implement a temporary split 50/50.
deploy-bot: action queued: route-split update -> {canary: v5.0.2=50%, v5.0.1-fallback=50%} for eu-central. change will apply in ~30s.
support-bot: customer-watch created and tagged #support; blurb draft queued.
pm-leo: draft blurb: "We paused the canary for v5.0.2 after a subset of /chat requests returned server errors. We routed a portion of traffic back to a fallback model variant while we investigate." ok to send on ops approval?
ops-ray: approve to send. tagging support for active watch.
sre-alex: route-split applied. initial effect: 502s dropped to 0.25% cluster-wide, nodepool-alpha errors down to 0.3%. p95 unchanged.
claire: that's promising. can we leave the split for a 10m observation window and then either resume full canary or rollback?
samir: agree. if 5xx stays <0.5% for 10m we resume. otherwise rollback to v5.0.1 (build 20260630.4).
pm-leo: note for release notes: block rollforward until postmortem if we end up rolling back. also prepare short customer-facing rollback message.
ops-ray: logging decision: reason=canary-5xx-subset, action=manual-hold+variant-split, rollback-if=10m sustained 5xx>0.5%, rollback-target=v5.0.1, comms=partial-fallback-sent
samir: thanks team. i'll update in 10m or sooner if it re-escalates. :hourglass:
